title: Composition of the Mahabharata and Ramayana
summary: The two great Sanskrit epics of India took shape over centuries. Reference works date the Mahabharata, a 100,000-verse tale of the Pandava-Kaurava war at Kurukshetra, to roughly 400 BCE to 400 CE, and the Ramayana, on Rama's exile and the recovery of Sita from Ravana, to between about 750 BCE and the 200s BCE. Tradition credits Vyasa and Valmiki.

uncertainty.note: Spans the earliest date stated for the Ramayana's current form (750 BCE, Encyclopedia of Religion) to the end of the Mahabharata window (c. 400 CE, Concise Oxford Dictionary of World Religions). Sources disagree: Mahabharata 500 BCE to 400 CE (Hiltebeitel) or 400 BCE to 200 CE (Oxford); Ramayana c. 300 BCE (Oxford) or the 5th century BCE (World History Encyclopedia). The epics grew over time and the dates are scholarly estimates.
